comment: Custom seccomp profile for the tier-2 url-preview container (open class url-preview-known-origin). Deny-by-default; the weston-terminal allowlist (bash + weston + weston-terminal + wayland libs + coreutils + less) PLUS the extra syscalls `curl` + glibc resolver need for an egress HTTP(S) fetch over the class-pinned slirp4netns network: sendmmsg/recvmmsg (glibc DNS), the AF_INET socket family (already permitted at the socket-syscall level; reachable here because --network slirp4netns is set, unlike the network=none classes). Measured deny-by-default superset (codex design fix 7), NOT podman's default.

syscalls.comment: Process lifecycle and job control (setpgid/setsid needed by bash job control, set_robust_list/rseq by glibc/pthread init, pidfd_open/pidfd_send_signal by libudev via weston)
File I/O. flock needed by libwayland-server for socket lock files. fsync by libglib. close_range by glibc/libglib (modern close-on-exec). statfs by bash.

Socket (wayland client/server, pipewire). socketpair needed by weston for internal IPC. Network=none at the podman level prevents AF_INET/AF_INET6 even though the syscall is allowed. sendmmsg/recvmmsg added for the glibc DNS resolver used by curl in the url-preview workload (egress fetch).
Epoll/poll (weston event loop). epoll_pwait/epoll_pwait2 used by glibc >= 2.35 and libwayland.
Signal handling (rt_sigsuspend needed by bash wait builtin, rt_sigpending by signal-safe cleanup paths)
Time and timers (weston event loop, animations)

User/group IDs. The set* variants are needed by podman's --userns=keep-id uid mapping; they are neutered by --cap-drop=ALL (no CAP_SETUID/SETGID) and --security-opt=no-new-privileges. getresuid/getresgid used by bash.

Misc: ioctl (terminal, DRM), futex (glibc threading), getrandom (weston), eventfd/signalfd (event loops), memfd/ftruncate/fallocate (wayland SHM), chmod/chown/umask (coreutils), inotify (weston config watch), prlimit64/getrlimit/setrlimit (glibc, bash ulimit). chown/fchown* neutered by --cap-drop=ALL (no CAP_CHOWN).

Explicitly denied high-risk syscalls (return EPERM, not ENOSYS like the default, so callers cannot mistake the deny for 'kernel too old'). Listed individually so auditors can see exactly what is blocked and why.
